english.title: Deprive / displace residential occupier from premises
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), unlawfully deprived **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), the residential occupier of premises, namely **(..SPECIFY PREMISES AND LOCATION..), of

english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(2) and (4) of the Protection from Eviction Act 1977.

english.notes:
(i) Proceedings for an offence under this Act may be instituted by the following authorities:
Councils of districts and London boroughs;Councils of Welsh counties and county boroughs;The Common Council of the City of London.
(iii) Section 1(2) provides a defence of reasonable belief that the residential occupier / s had ceased to reside in the premises.(ii) A person may not be convicted of this offence, in respect of any conduct, if a civil financial penalty has been imposed by a local authority as an alternative to prosecution under section 1A.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6 / 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

(i) On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
(ii) The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.
